Transcribed from two full-resolution photographs of this branch's own touch-screen ticket machine, taken 2026-03; the 2025-06 shot of the same screen carries identical prices on every overlapping line (かけそば ¥450, もりそば ¥450, 特もり ¥800, ごまだれ ¥550, 二色 ¥650, 釜玉 ¥450, とろろ ¥700, 温玉納豆 ¥750, 天ぷら ¥650, all four sets, all four tempura, all seven toppings, beer ¥350), so these figures have held for at least nine months. The machine rotates two or three seasonal slots: the 2026-03 screen carried 彩り野菜の鴨せいろ／鴨南蛮そば at ¥950 marked 新発売, while the 2025-06 screen instead carried 夏野菜のペペロンそば ¥850 and たぬきそば 冷/温 ¥520 — those three are listed at the bottom of this menu and flagged, because they may or may not be on the machine on the day you visit. The operator's own page for this branch (株式会社フォーユー, 十割蕎麦 さがたに 渋谷東急本店前店) confirms the address 渋谷区道玄坂2-25-7 プラザ道玄坂1F, 21 counter seats, hours 7:00–22:00 Mon–Fri and 10:00–21:00 weekends/holidays, closed 1–3 January, NO credit cards but e-money and QR accepted, and free wakame with any bowl. GLUTEN, IN ONE LINE: the noodles are 十割 (100% buckwheat, stone-milled on the premises) and the shop states nothing about its 打ち粉 dusting flour; the tsuyu is a soba tsuyu, i.e. soy-sauce based; the same small counter kitchen deep-fries tempura to order and serves wheat-roux Japanese curry. Nobody should treat this as a gluten-free soba shop. The operator does publish its dashi: 冷つゆ is 昆布と3種類のブレンド節, 温つゆ 昆布と4種類のブレンド節 — kombu plus blended fish flakes, which settles the vegan question for every bowl served with tsuyu.

items.en: Cold 100% buckwheat soba on a tray with dipping tsuyu — the shop's core product at the price it is famous for
items.note: 十割 (100% buckwheat) noodles milled in-store on a stone mill, so the noodle itself carries no wheat flour — but the shop does not say what its 打ち粉 (board dusting flour) is, and the tsuyu is a soba tsuyu, which is soy-sauce based and therefore wheat by default. The operator's own page gives the cold tsuyu as 昆布と3種類のブレンド節 — kombu plus three blended fish flakes — so it is also not vegan. Ask for no tsuyu and it is still not coeliac-safe because of the dusting flour and the shared boiling water.
Double portion of the もりそば. Same wheat and dashi caveats.

The hot tsuyu is the shop's 温つゆ, 昆布と4種類のブレンド節 (kombu plus four blended fish flakes) per the operator's own page — bonito-family flakes, so not vegan — and a hot soba broth is built on soy sauce, so wheat. Noodles are 十割 but see the dusting-flour caveat on もりそば.

items.ja: 冷かけそば（ぶっかけそば）

items.note: Cold tsuyu poured over the noodles — kombu and three fish flakes, on a soy base. Same gluten position as かけそば.

items.en: Cold soba with a sesame dipping sauce (the machine's English: 'Cold soba with sesame sauce')
items.note: A ごまだれ is sesame paste let down with soy sauce and usually dashi — two wheat routes and one animal route on top of the noodle caveats. The shop publishes no recipe for it.

The machine's English caption on this button reads 'Cold soba with sesame sauce', which is the same caption it prints on ごまだれそば — apparently copied — so what the second 'colour' actually is (a second noodle, or a second dip) is NOT evidenced and is not guessed at here. ¥100 over the plain もり and ¥100 over the ごまだれ. Same noodle and tsuyu caveats.

items.en: Hot soba tossed with raw egg — the machine prints ※つゆなし, no tsuyu
items.note: The one bowl on the machine that is explicitly served WITHOUT tsuyu, which removes the soy-sauce route — but it is still not gluten-free: the noodles are lifted straight from the shop's boiling water and the shop states nothing about its dusting flour, and the same kitchen fries tempura. Raw egg, so not vegan.

items.en: Cold soba topped with grated mountain yam
items.note: Grated yam is plant-only, but it is normally slackened with dashi and the bowl comes with the shop's fish-flake tsuyu. Wheat via the tsuyu.

items.en: Hot soba topped with grated mountain yam

items.en: Cold soba with natto, a soft-boiled egg and shredded nori — cold only

items.en: Cold soba topped with vegetable tempura (kakiage)
items.note: Tempura batter is wheat flour, fried in the shop's own fryer — the operator advertises 揚げたて, fried to order on site. This is the dish that makes the whole kitchen a wheat kitchen. Batter usually contains egg as well.

items.en: Hot soba topped with vegetable tempura
items.note: Wheat batter plus the fish-flake hot tsuyu.

Japanese curry is thickened with a wheat-flour roux and this one is let down with the soy-based hot tsuyu — wheat twice over. The shop does not list what meat is in it, so vegan is 'ask' rather than an assumption, but a shop curry normally carries pork or beef.

items.note: The operator's own page states 「お蕎麦と相性抜群のわかめをいつでも無料サービスしています」. Salted rehydrated wakame is seaweed and salt — plant-only and with no gluten grain in it — but it sits in a self-serve tub with shared tongs in a shop that batters and fries tempura a metre away, so it is 'ask' rather than 'gf'.

items.en: A pot of the sesame sauce, as a topping
items.note: Sesame paste thinned with soy sauce, usually with dashi. Wheat via the soy.
Grated yam is a vegetable, but soba shops normally loosen it with dashi or tsuyu, both of which would put fish and soy sauce into it. Not stated. The dearest topping on the machine.
A shell egg cracked into the bowl, nothing added — the topping carries no wheat. Egg, so not vegan, and the bowl underneath is still not gluten-free.
An onsen egg is egg and hot water, but it is very often supplied in a pack with a soy-sauce tare. The machine says nothing, so 'ask'.

The beans themselves are soybeans and bacteria — vegan and wheat-free — but natto is served with its sachet of tare, which is soy sauce (wheat) and commonly carries bonito extract. Whether the shop uses the sachet is not stated.

It is still 'ask' rather than 'gf' because it is scooped in a kitchen that batters and deep-fries tempura to order and serves a wheat-roux curry; ask for a clean scoop and take nothing poured over it.

tokyo_teuchi_soba_watanabe_han.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Every price here is transcribed from the shop's OWN site (a Google Sites at sites.google.com/view/teuchisobawatanabe), re-fetched live on 2026-08-25 — the 蕎麦, 肴 and 酒 pages are three separate priced lists and the shop also publishes a メニュー詳細 page describing what is in each bowl dish by dish, which is where nearly every ingredient note below comes from. The site is currently maintained: its お知らせ page carries a 2026 closure notice for 8月11日(火)～16日(日). Shop's own details: 東京都新宿区西新宿1-12-10 八洋ビル1階, 03-3348-9126, Mon–Sat 11:00–21:30, closed Sundays, CASH ONLY (クレジットカード利用不可・現金のみ), all seats non-smoking, 47 seats. Trading over 40 years — 「４０年以上 新宿と共に歩んできた渡邊」. TWO THINGS A COELIAC MUST READ. (1) おかめそば contains お麩 — fu is pure wheat gluten, and nothing in the dish's name says so; the shop's own description lists 「しいたけ・お麩・かまぼこ・だし巻きたまご・たけのこ」. (2) The shop nowhere states its buckwheat-to-wheat ratio: this is 手打蕎麦 (hand-cut), not 十割, and Japanese hand-cut soba is normally blended with wheat flour, so the noodles themselves are presumed to contain wheat — on top of the board's dusting flour, the soy-based tsuyu and a tempura fryer that runs to order. Also note 揚げ玉 (tenkasu, fried wheat batter) hides in 冷山菜そば and ちからそば, and the 蕎麦焼酎そば湯割り is cut with そば湯, the water the noodles were boiled in.

items.en: The plain cold soba — the shop says this is what to order on a first visit, and the one to finish on after drinking
items.note: The house's own recommendation for a first-timer and the cheapest bowl on the card. Not gluten-free: hand-cut soba at a shop that does not state a 十割 claim is normally blended with wheat flour, the noodles are dusted with 打ち粉 and boiled in shared water, and the dipping tsuyu is soy-sauce based. Vegan is 'ask' because a Tokyo soba house tsuyu is normally built on katsuobushi dashi; the shop publishes no recipe.

items.en: Seiro with nori laid over it, served with a quail egg
items.note: The shop's own description: 「せいろにのりを乗せたお蕎麦です(うずら付き)」 — the quail egg makes it non-vegan, and ¥100 is the whole price of the nori. Wheat as per せいろ.

items.en: Two seiro stacked — the regulars' favourite, for when one is not enough
items.note: 「常連さん一番人気です」 per the shop. Double portion of the plain seiro; same wheat and dashi position.

items.en: Cold soba with a separate dish of grated daikon — dip the soba in it, or mix the daikon into the tsuyu and pour it over
items.note: The shop notes the daikon is not a hot variety (「大根は辛くないです」) and calls it a summer bowl. Grated daikon is plant-only; the tsuyu is the wheat and the probable dashi.

items.en: Cold soba with grated mountain yam served alongside, dusted with aonori — comes with a quail egg
items.note: Quail egg (うずら付き), so not vegan. The shop warns not to tip all the tsuyu into the tororo at once. Wheat via noodles and tsuyu.

items.en: Cold soba topped with mountain vegetables, grated daikon, spring onion and tenkasu
items.note: 揚げ玉 (tenkasu) is fried tempura batter — WHEAT, sitting visibly on top of an otherwise vegetable bowl. The sansai are usually preserved in a soy or salt brine. The shop's pitch: if you have never eaten sansai, try it.

items.en: Cold soba with natto, grated daikon, spring onion, raw egg and nori — mix the lot together
items.note: Raw egg per the shop's own description, so not vegan. Natto is served with a soy tare. Wheat as per せいろ.

items.en: Cold soba with whitebait, grated daikon, wakame and shiitake
items.note: Whitebait — fish. Wheat as per せいろ.

items.en: A larger serving of the same noodles under two different garnishes (nori and katsuobushi), with tororo on the side
items.note: The shop is explicit that the noodle is the same and only the 薬味 differ: 「のり・かつおぶし」. Katsuobushi (dried bonito) puts fish directly on the plate, not just in the broth. Portion is bigger than a seiro.

items.ja: きのこ玉子とじせいろ
items.en: Cold soba dipped into a hot mushroom broth thickened with beaten egg; noodles arrive in three piles but are all the same, about two seiro's worth
items.note: Egg in the dip, so not vegan. The hot dip is a soy-and-dashi broth — wheat.

items.en: Cold soba with tempura on the side — two prawns, carrot, sweet potato and nori, fried to order
items.note: The shop lists the exact tempura: 「えび2本・にんじん・さつまいも・のり」, fried after you order (「ご注文が入ってから天ぷらを揚げる」). Wheat batter and prawns. This is the fryer that makes the rest of the kitchen a wheat kitchen.

items.en: 天せいろ with nori over the noodles
items.note: The shop jokes that the only difference from 天せいろ is the nori. Wheat batter, prawns.

items.en: Cold soba dipped into a hot duck broth; about two seiro's worth of noodles in three piles
items.note: Duck. The dip is a sweetened soy-and-dashi broth. Dearest bowl on the card.

items.en: An extra seiro of noodles — the shop does not do 大盛, so this is how you get more; noodles ONLY, ask staff if you want more tsuyu or garnish
items.note: Useful line: the shop states 「渡邊には大盛はないので」 and that this comes as noodles alone, orderable up front or after you have started, with any dish. Vegan 'ask' because plain soba noodles are normally just flour and water — the shop does not publish the ingredients — and because no tsuyu comes with it, this is the one item where the dashi question does not arise. It is still not gluten-free: the noodle is presumed wheat-blended and it is dusted and boiled with everything else.

items.en: Hot soba in broth — 'the one where you really taste the tsuyu'
items.note: The shop's whole description is about the broth. A hot soba tsuyu is soy sauce, mirin and dashi — wheat, and near-certainly bonito.

items.en: Hot soba under nori — the only hot bowl garnished with wasabi instead of spring onion; the shop's recommended nightcap after drinking
items.note: Shop's own note: 「通常温かいおそばの薬味はねぎですが、花巻そばにはわさびが付いてきます」. Nori and wasabi are plant-only; the broth is the wheat and the dashi.

items.en: Hot soba bound with beaten egg — the shop calls it the bowl you want when your stomach is off
items.note: Egg. Soy-based broth.

items.en: Hot soba with two grilled mochi, bamboo shoot, spring onion, shiitake and tenkasu
items.note: 揚げ玉 (tenkasu) again — fried WHEAT batter, listed by the shop itself among the toppings. The mochi is glutinous rice, which despite the English name contains no gluten, but that is irrelevant here because the tenkasu and the noodles do.

items.en: Hot soba loaded with shiitake, FU (wheat-gluten cake), kamaboko fish cake, rolled dashi omelette and bamboo shoot, arranged as a face
items.note: READ THIS ONE. The shop's own ingredient list is 「しいたけ・お麩・かまぼこ・だし巻きたまご・たけのこ」. 麩 (fu) is PURE WHEAT GLUTEN — it looks like a light little sponge and is the single most concentrated gluten on the menu; nothing in the dish's name warns you. Also carries egg and fish cake, so it is not vegan either. Kamaboko is normally bound with starch and the omelette is made with dashi.

items.en: Hot soba under grated mountain yam, with two quail eggs to drop in as you go
items.note: Two quail eggs per the shop (「うずらが2つも付いてくる」), so not vegan. Wheat via noodles and broth.

items.en: Hot soba with mushrooms, bound with beaten egg
items.note: Egg. Soy-based broth.

items.en: Hot soba with grated mountain yam and mountain vegetables
items.note: Yam and sansai are plant-only; the broth is the wheat and the likely bonito. Sansai are usually brine- or soy-preserved.

items.en: Hot soba with whitebait, grated daikon melting into the broth, shiitake and wakame
items.note: Whitebait — fish.

items.en: Hot soba with yuba (soy-milk skin) and shiso leaf, garnished with wasabi
items.note: The most plant-forward hot bowl here — yuba is nothing but soy milk skin, and shiso and wasabi are leaves — so the only animal question is the broth's dashi, which the shop does not publish. Gluten is unaffected: soy-based broth and wheat-blended noodles.

items.en: Hot soba with duck and spring onion in a broth the shop wants you to drink to the bottom
items.note: Duck. Soy-based broth.

items.en: Hot soba with a whole sweet-simmered herring on top
items.note: Herring, simmered in soy and sugar — the fish itself is glazed in wheat-containing soy sauce as well as sitting in a soy broth.

items.en: Hot soba with the tempura served separately so it stays crisp — same tempura as 天せいろ (two prawns, carrot, sweet potato, nori)
items.note: Wheat batter, prawns. The shop points out you can keep it crisp on the side or dunk it.

items.en: Tempura on the side, and the soba itself bound with beaten egg
items.note: Wheat batter, prawns, egg.

items.en: Tempura on the side, with grated daikon stirred through the soba
items.note: Wheat batter, prawns. Joint dearest hot bowl.

items.en: Chicken and egg over rice, in a lacquer box
items.note: Chicken and egg simmered in a soy-and-dashi broth poured over the rice — the sauce is the wheat.

items.en: Tempura over rice, in a lacquer box
items.note: Wheat batter, prawns, and a 重 tare is soy sauce and mirin.

items.en: Soba rolled in nori and cut like sushi
items.note: It is the shop's own noodle rolled in nori, so the noodle's presumed wheat blend applies; the fillings are not published, and a soba-zushi roll commonly carries egg or fish. Ask what is in it.

items.en: Sobagaki — buckwheat flour whisked with hot water into a soft dumpling, eaten with the tsuyu and wasabi
items.note: THE ONE TO ASK ABOUT. Sobagaki is classically nothing but buckwheat flour and hot water — no noodle, no cutting board, no dusting flour — so it is the only dish here that could conceivably be wheat-free, and it is worth asking whether the shop's そば粉 is pure and whether it can be served without the soy tsuyu. It is still 'ask', not 'gf': the shop publishes no ingredient or allergen statement, wheat flour is worked in the same kitchen, and the dipping tsuyu is soy sauce. Vegan 'ask' on the same tsuyu question; the dumpling itself is plant-only.
Wasabi stems are a vegetable, but 茎漬け is cured either in sake lees or in soy sauce and the shop does not say which — soy sauce would make it wheat. Joint cheapest snack.

items.en: The shop's own soba, deep-fried into crisp sticks
items.note: Fried noodles: the presumed wheat blend in the noodle, plus the tempura fryer. Normally just salted, so the vegan question is only whether it is seasoned with anything.

items.en: Skewers glazed with sweet miso and grilled
items.note: Two hidden questions and the shop answers neither: dengaku miso may be 麦味噌 (BARLEY miso — gluten, and barley is not even on Japan's statutory allergen list, so no label will warn you), and a 玉味噌 style glaze is normally enriched with egg yolk and sometimes dashi. What is under the glaze (konjac, tofu, aubergine) is not stated either.
Fish. Served to be splashed with soy sauce, which is where the wheat would come in — ask for it plain or bring tamari.

items.ja: うずらの玉子の味噌漬け
items.note: Egg, so not vegan. The miso cure is the gluten question — barley miso is common and unlabelled.
Depends entirely on which pickles: 醤油漬け and many commercial tsukemono seasonings carry soy sauce (wheat) and some carry bonito extract. Nothing is published.

items.en: Sliced kamaboko fish cake with wasabi
items.note: Steamed fish paste — not vegan. Kamaboko is bound with starch which is usually potato but can be wheat, and it is eaten dipped in soy sauce.
Fish paste, and commercial satsuma-age is routinely bound with wheat flour and then deep-fried; here it also meets the tempura fryer.
Egg, and the dashi is the point of the dish — a dashimaki is seasoned with 白だし or だし醤油, both soy-sauce based, so this is wheat as well as fish. A classic 'looks safe, isn't' item.

items.en: Miso grilled on a spatula, with duck meat mixed in
items.note: Duck, so not vegan. Miso may be barley; a 焼き味噌 is also usually let down with mirin or sake. The classic thing to nurse a sake over at a soba house.

items.en: Tochio abura-age — the thick, palm-sized fried tofu from Niigata, grilled and served with garnish
items.note: Tochio-age is soybeans, water and coagulant fried in oil, so the block itself is plant-only and grain-free — but it is served in this kitchen, which means shared fryer oil with wheat tempura, and it is normally finished with spring onion, ginger and a splash of soy sauce, and very often 鰹節. Ask for it plain and ask about the oil.

items.ja: 貝柱とこんにゃくのピリ辛煮
items.romaji: kaibashira to konnyaku no pirikara ni
items.en: Scallop adductor and konjac simmered spicy
items.note: Shellfish, and anything 煮 in a Japanese kitchen is simmered in soy sauce and mirin — wheat.

Yuba is the skin lifted off simmering soy milk — soybeans and water, nothing else, and a genuinely plant-based plate. Both flags are 'ask' only because of what comes with it: yuba sashi is dipped in soy sauce (wheat) or, at some shops, in だし醤油, which adds bonito too. Ask for salt or bring tamari and this is one of the better options here for either diet.

items.en: Herring simmered slowly in sweet soy
items.note: Fish, and 甘露煮 means simmered in soy sauce and sugar — wheat.
The yuba is plant-only but the batter is wheat flour and tempura batter usually contains egg. Everything the yuba sashi has going for it is undone by the batter.

items.en: Shojin-age — vegetables-only tempura, no fish or meat
items.note: 'Shojin' means the temple-cuisine convention of no animal flesh, so the contents are vegetables — but tempura batter is wheat flour and commonly egg, and it goes into the same oil as the prawn tempura, so it is neither gluten-free nor reliably vegan.
The dearest thing on the whole card. Wheat batter; the shop's tempura line-up includes prawns.

Sake is brewed from rice, water, rice-koji and yeast — no barley, no wheat, and no animal ingredient. It is one of the few genuinely gluten-free things a coeliac can drink in a Japanese restaurant, and unlike beer, 麦焼酎 or a highball it is safe here. (Anything served in the same glassware is a non-issue; the risk in this shop is food, not drink.)

items.en: Chilled local sake — brand not stated on the site
items.note: Sake, i.e. rice and koji — gluten-free and plant-based. The shop does not name the brewery on its site, so ask what is pouring.

items.ja: ノンアルコールビール
items.note: Removing the alcohol does not remove the barley malt. Non-alcoholic beer is NOT gluten-free and this trips people up constantly.
Barley malt.
Barley malt.

items.en: Buckwheat shochu cut with soba-yu, the cloudy water the noodles were boiled in
items.note: A trap that looks like the coeliac's drink and is the opposite. そば湯 is literally the noodle water: it is thick with the starch that came off the noodles and the 打ち粉 dusted on them, so if there is any wheat in either — and at a shop that does not claim 十割 there almost certainly is — it is dissolved in this glass. The shochu itself is distilled from buckwheat but is often made with a barley koji. Plant-based, so vegan.
Grape wine contains no gluten grain. Vegan is 'ask' because wines are often fined with isinglass, gelatin or egg white, and the shop does not name the wine.

items.ja: 手打生蕎麦 4人前 化粧箱入り（年越蕎麦）
